business_summary.text: Azad Engineering manufactures critical rotating components for gas, steam and nuclear turbines, aerospace and defence parts, and precision assemblies for oil and gas, supplying global OEMs such as GE, Siemens, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Baker Hughes.

call_points.text: Substantive revenue from new lines is guided to show from Q3FY27, with Q2 described as machines running at full throttle.
Baker Hughes 7,600 sq m facility inaugurated April 2026, the fourth dedicated OEM plant after Mitsubishi, GE and Siemens.
Civil construction of remaining units to finish this fiscal; post-FY29 capex quantum deferred to next quarter.
Turbojet engine delivered to GTRE; weapon testing 4-6 weeks away, then worthiness certification for production.
Hot-section facility for Mitsubishi is 7-8 months from establishment, then qualification; other OEMs already interested.
First Rolls-Royce civil engine qualification parts to be delivered within this quarter.
Raw material fell to 5% of sales from about 12% last year on domestic supplier qualification and freight savings.
Export receivables to be naturally hedged via foreign-currency loans and bill discounting by Q4.
Management named execution complexity, running factories, hiring and contracts together, as the main challenge.
FY27 top-line growth guided at approximately 25% plus, on qualified products only.
EBITDA margin guidance of 33-35% plus, with potential upside from continuous improvements.
Four of eight dedicated plants commissioned; balance four to be completed in FY27.
Mitsubishi Heavy Industries 8-year single-source contract for hot section nozzle vanes; value not disclosed.
Rolls-Royce first qualification batch expected in H2 FY27; supply momentum from Q4 FY27 or early FY28.
FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 37.4%, helped by backward integration reducing outsourcing cost.
Gross debt ₹457 Cr, net debt ₹272 Cr; treasury ₹184 Cr including ₹160 Cr QIP proceeds.
Saudi Arabia Baker Hughes capex timelines shifted; management prioritising current plants.
ATGG engine order count and delivery schedule withheld as part of a national defence programme.

exceptions: fine or penalty: Goods and Services Tax Department (Penalty imposed)

guidance.statement: Top line growth of approximately 25% plus for FY27, on qualified products only
Inventory days to reduce to closer to 200 days in H1 and 160-170 days in H2
Long-term annual revenue growth guidance reiterated at over 25% with industry-leading profitability maintained
EBITDA margin calculation window held at 32-35%
Working capital days targeted near 200 in H1FY27 and 160-180 in H2FY27

industry: Industrials > Capital Goods > Electrical Equipment > Heavy Electrical Equipment

operating_notes.text: Order book of ₹6,500 Cr is split roughly $400 million Energy, $200 million+ Aerospace & Defence and $100 million+ Oil & Gas.
Oil & Gas revenue was under ₹10 Cr in FY26, largely qualification work with Baker Hughes; management expects material ramp-up in FY27.
Four of eight dedicated OEM plants commissioned; balance four to be completed in FY27.
Each of the eight dedicated plants at Tuniki Bollaram is poised to generate ₹150-180 Cr at full utilisation, about ₹1,200 Cr in total.
Debtor days are around 170-180 and are targeted down to 90 via bill discounting facilities.
Hiring runs at roughly 150-200 people a month through a 90-day training programme to build bench strength.

holders.name: AXIS MUTUAL FUND TRUSTEE LIMITED A/C AXIS MUTUAL F

timeline.summary: Azad Engineering's Q4 FY26 call (16 May 2026) reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹603 Cr, up 32%, and an order book of ₹6,500 Cr, with an 8-year Mitsubishi Heavy Industries contract for hot section nozzle vanes.

Azad Engineering's Q1FY27 call (Aug 8, 2026) reported standalone revenue up 26.8% YoY to ₹170.5 Cr at a 37.6% EBITDA margin, and flagged delivery of India's first indigenous turbojet engine to GTRE/DRDO.
